newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close strongly up on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close strongly up on fund buying.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures closed sharply higher, led by soymeal, on fund buying which started in the corn pit and finished in a relentless manner, traders said.
"It's all funds and technical today, we hit stops and also locals bought it," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter

The soy complex also was boosted by a surprisingly high USDA weekly export inspections report. USDA said soybean export inspections in the week ended February 13 totalled roughly 35 million bushels, well above trade expectations for 20 million to 24 million bushels.
Soymeal also found support from Friday's USDA seven state Cattle on Feed Report which showed the January placements of cattle on feed up 25 percent from a year ago, a tally well above expectations.
Reports of excessive rainfall in areas of Brazil also lent support and prompted speculation on the CBOT floor that Brazilian harvest and exports would be slowed.
Soymeal closed $2.70 to $7.40 per ton higher, with March up $7.40 at $255.60 a ton. Soyoil closed 0.12 to 0.26 cent per lb higher, with March up 0.26 at 23.93 cents.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 33,000 contracts, above the 20,476 traded Friday.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 28,000 contracts, above the 19,453 traded Friday.
